question.text: In a photoelectric experiment, a parallel beam of monochromatic light with the power of <math> <mrow> <mn>200</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>W</mtext></mrow> </math> is incident on a perfectly absorbing cathode of work function <math><mn>6.25</mn><mi> </mi><mi>eV</mi></math>. The frequency of light is just above the threshold frequency so that the photoelectrons are emitted with negligible kinetic energy. Assume that the photoelectron emission efficiency is 100%. A potential difference of <math> <mrow> <mn>500</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>V</mtext></mrow> </math> is applied between the cathode and the anode. All the emitted electrons are incident normally on the anode and are absorbed. The anode experiences a force <math><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mn> N</mn></math> due to the impact of the electrons. The value of <math> <mi>n</mi> </math> is __________. Mass of the electron <math><msub><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>31</mn></mrow></msup><mi> kg</mi><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi> </mi><mn>1.0</mn><mi> </mi><mi>eV</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mi> J</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Power =Nhν

N= number of photons per second

Since KE=0,hν=ϕ

200=N6.25×1.6×10-19  Joule

N=2006.25×1.6×10-19

As photon is just above threshold frequency KEmax is zero and they are accelerated by potential difference of 500 V

KEf=q∆V

P22m=q∆V⇒P=2mq∆V

Since efficiency is 100%, number of electrons emitted is equal to number of photons falling per second as electrons are completely absorbed, force exerted nmv

= 2006.25×1.6×10-19×29×10-31×1.6×10-19×500

= 3×200×10-25×16006.25×1.6×10-19=2×406.25×1.6×10-4×3=24 × 10 −4

n=24
